Certificate:
- Number: R76/2006-NL1-12.02
- Scheme: The certificate number format "R76/2006-NL1-12.02" — this is a standard OIML certificate. Scheme A vs B... Actually OIML-CS has scheme A and B. This is from 2012, before the OIML CS. The rule says scheme (A|B). Hmm. Older certificates... The certificate is issued by NMi as OIML Issuing Authority NL1. I could leave scheme out or set it... The schema says scheme (A|B). Since it's not stated in the document, per rule 8 (don't fabricate), omit it. But the schema lists it... "If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." So omit scheme.

- type_designations: ["LP7510A", "LP7510B"]
- module_designation: null? The type is an Indicator — module designation isn't stated. Omit or null. For load cells there's "Analog load cell". Not applicable here — omit.

Model family: cert covers 2 model variants LP7510A and LP7510B. But do any characteristics vary per model? The characteristics page lists:
- n ≤ 3000 for class (III) or n ≤ 1000 for class (IIII) — varies by accuracy class, not model.
- p_i: 0.5
- min input impedance 300 Ω
- max input impedance 1050 Ω
- signal voltage per verification scale interval ≥ 3 μV
- temperature range -10°C / +40°C

No per-model variation given, so model_level not needed. Should I include model_family? Rule: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. It covers LP7510A and LP7510B — two variants. Include:
"model_family": {"family_name": null, "models": [{"model_id": "LP7510A"}, {"model_id": "LP7510B"}]}

But no attributes vary per model, so model_level stays empty/omitted.

Characteristics type_level:
- max_number_of_verification_scale_intervals: varies by accuracy class — this could be config_level with axis "accuracy_class". Values: condition "(III)" → 3000, condition "(IIII)" → 1000. Config-level: axis "accuracy_class".
- applied_error_fraction_pi: 0.5, unit null
- minimum_input_impedance: 300 Ω
- maximum_input_impedance: 1050 Ω
- signal_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: {min: 3, max: null}, unit "μV"
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"

Test reports:

- {id: "NMi-11200243-02", date: "2012-03-01", pages: 16, role: "test_report"}

Revision history: none present. Omit.

Footnotes: none.

The scheme field — schema says scheme (A|B). Not present; omit.

unit_id: leave null unless certain. Units like Ω, μV, °C — I could guess "u:ohm", "u:uV" but rule says leave null unless certain. I'll leave null.

For config_level entry shape: {attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}}. The structured value form applies: values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So:

"config_level": [
  {
    "attribute": "max_number_of_verification_scale_intervals",
    "axis": "accuracy_class",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "III", "value": {"value": {"min": null, "max": 3000}, "unit_symbol": null, "footnote_markers": []}},
      {"condition": "IIII", "value": {"value": {"min": null, "max": 1000}, "unit_symbol": null, "footnote_markers": []}}
    ]
  }
]

Hmm, "n ≤ 3000" — value is a bound ≤3000. Structured: value {min: null, max: 3000}? Or just 3000 as the maximum permitted count. "The maximum number of verification scale intervals will be: n ≤ 3000". The value itself is the maximum allowed n. I'd say value: 3000 with attribute max_number_of_verification_scale_intervals. That's cleaner: the attribute already encodes "maximum". So value 3000 and 1000.

Structured values strict: every characteristic value must be an object with value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. So:

"config_level": [
  {
    "attribute": "maximum_number_of_verification_scale_intervals",
    "axis": "accuracy_class",
    "values": [
      {"condition": "III", "value": 3000, "unit_symbol": null},
      {"condition": "IIII", "value": 1000, "unit_symbol": null}
    ]
  }
]

Note example in rules shows config_level values as {condition, value} with same structured form. In rule 5: "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

Type-level characteristics:

"applied_error_fraction_pi": {"value": 0.5, "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": []}
"minimum_input_impedance": {"value": 300, "unit_symbol": "Ω", ...}
"maximum_input_impedance": {"value": 1050, "unit_symbol": "Ω", ...}
"signal_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval": {"value": {"min": null, "max": 3}, "unit_symbol": "μV", ...} — wait, ≥3 μV means minimum 3 μV. So value {min: 3, max: null}. Open-ended lower bound: ≥1000 → {min: 1000, max: null}. Yes, {min: 3, max: null}.
